Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Senegal has a fully deployed nationwide biometric national ID system. The ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card (ENBIC/CEDEAO card) has been issued since 2016 — Senegal was the first ECOWAS country to do so. The Directorate of File Automation (DAF) under the Ministry of Interior manages the biometric population register and issues national ID cards, passports, and residency documents. As of 2025 approximately 10 million citizens (>90% of adults aged 15+) hold a biometric card. A new digital identity layer (INN – Identifiant Numérique National) was launched in 2022 with UNDP support as part of the Digital Senegal 2025 strategy. The 2025 'New Deal Technologique' targets a unique biometric digital ID for all sectoral uses by 2034.

revision_notes: Confirmed, Code 5 stands. Senegal's ECOWAS Biometric ID Card (ENBIC/CNI), issued nationwide by DAF since 2016, is a foundational digital ID covering an estimated 90%+ of adults 15+ (~10m cardholders per an Institute of Development Studies/African Digital Rights Network report, 2025 data, reported by The Conversation, March 2026). A February 2026 data breach briefly halted new-card issuance, but Le Soleil (7 April 2026) confirms DAF resumed production 'à l'échelle nationale' from 1 April 2026, which corroborates rather than undermines nationwide operational status. A separate digital-identity layer (INN) is still under development to 2034 (New Deal Technologique) but this is additive, not a precondition for the foundational ID's 'fully deployed' status. biometricupdate.com is an authoritative specialist industry publication despite the redteam flag, not an off-topic aggregator.

Voter-registration reporting (Feb 2025, 2.9m cardholders not yet on the electoral roll, against ~7.3m registered voters and an 18m population) is consistent with, but does not independently prove, this coverage level.
